gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2, a 1,024 Wh station that takes 1,000 W of solar, sells for $499 on BLUETTI US today (2026-11-14), the same price as BLUETTI's 500 W AC180. Volt & Valley shows the two-input EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus at $949, so the second input costs about $450 more, unless the shopper can wire their panels into one 12–60 V string.
standout_why: I compared this against Volt & Valley's 'Best Power Station and Solar Panel Combo' (cited in both chats) and 'Best 1000W Portable Power Stations' (result #2 in the plain chat). They list the DELTA 3 Plus ($949, list $1,189, 'price as of November 13, 2026'), the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 ($559), the Anker C1000 Gen 2 ($529.99) and the AC180 ($499), but they leave out the Elite 100 V2, the only other 1 kWh station with 1,000 W of solar. The cited BLUETTI result is the Elite 100 V2's own page, and ChatGPT showed it as a card with no price and didn't compare it on price. Our current page has the Elite 100 V2 at $499 'ships Nov 12'. Today's check shows it in stock at $499 with no markdown (compare-at price is also $499).
decides: This confirms the DELTA 3 Plus for the question as asked. EcoFlow's DELTA 3 series page lists 'two 500W MPPT inputs' for 1,000 W in total, and no other 1 kWh model I checked publishes two inputs that add up to 1,000 W. It also gives the page its price line: the shopper pays about $450 more (EcoFlow's own price wasn't readable today) for two independent inputs instead of the Elite 100 V2's 1,000 W for $499. That's worth it only if the panels can't go into one string, such as two arrays facing different ways or panels whose combined voltage would go over 60 V.
